descriptionChirho: Aramaic adjective רַבְרְבָן (rabreban) used attributively to modify nouns, meaning 'great' or 'mighty' in descriptions of significant entities such as kingdoms, beasts, or persons in Daniel. Eng 'great,' Spa 'grandes,' Hin 'बड़े,' Arb 'عَظِيمَةٌ,' Kor '큰,' Swa 'wakubwa.' Functions as a standard adjective qualifying a following or preceding noun within the clause.

Aramaic adjective רַבְרְבָן (rabreban) used substantively to denote 'great things' or 'mighty deeds,' functioning as a noun rather than modifying another noun. Eng 'great things,' Spa 'grandes cosas,' Hin 'बड़ी बातें,' Arb 'بِعَظَائِمَ,' Kor '큰것들을,' Swa 'mambo makubwa.' The Arabic uses the distinct nominal form عَظَائِم (great deeds/wonders), and Korean adds the nominalizer 것 (thing), confirming the substantive usage as a separate sense from the attributive adjective.
